title: Le feng shui de Nathalie  (Nathalie's Feng Shui)

segments.t: Mathias escorts Nathalie Baye to his old office suite, only to find the entire floor sublet to busy lawyers. Horrified by their cramped workspace, Nathalie impulsively begins reorganizing their desks with feng shui principles just as Andrea arrives to intervene. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Bienvenue dans mon ancien bureau, chère Nathalie.
On dirait plutôt un corral d'avocats!
L'agence a dû sous-louer cet étage entier.
Il faut faire circuler l'énergie ici!
Une belle plante verte changera toute l'ambiance.
Attention Nathalie, ce n'est pas votre travail.
Qui a déjà entendu parler du feng shui?
Nathalie! Que faites-vous dans cette pièce?
J'aide ces pauvres avocats à mieux respirer.
Mathias, tu essaies encore de voler mes clients?
J'offre simplement un conseil amical à Nathalie.
Andréa, j'adore votre grande énergie formidable.
Mais pour ce film, je préfère Camille.
Camille? C'est une excellente idée pour vous!
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Bienvenue dans mon ancien bureau, chère Nathalie.
'Welcome to my former office, dear Nathalie.' Mathias welcomes the actress into ASK. The adjective 'ancien' placed before a noun denotes former status.
On dirait plutôt un corral d'avocats!
'It looks more like a lawyers' corral!' Nathalie compares the open desks to a cattle pen. The noun 'corral' refers humorously to an enclosure.
L'agence a dû sous-louer cet étage entier.
'The agency had to sublet this entire floor.' Mathias explains the financial sublet. The verb 'sous-louer' means to sublet space.
Il faut faire circuler l'énergie ici!
'We must circulate the energy here!' Nathalie invokes harmonious energy flow. The causative verb 'faire circuler' means to cause to move or flow.
Une belle plante verte changera toute l'ambiance.
'A nice green plant will change the whole ambiance.' Nathalie introduces natural decor. The noun phrase 'plante verte' denotes a houseplant.
Attention Nathalie, ce n'est pas votre travail.
'Careful Nathalie, this is not your job.' Mathias warns her against interfering with staff. The warning interjection 'attention' urges caution.
Qui a déjà entendu parler du feng shui?
'Who has already heard of feng shui?' Nathalie addresses the astonished lawyers. The idiom 'entendre parler de' means to hear about something.
Nathalie! Que faites-vous dans cette pièce?
'Nathalie! What are you doing in this room?' Andrea bursts into the suite out of breath. The noun 'piece' refers to a room inside a building.
J'aide ces pauvres avocats à mieux respirer.
'I am helping these poor lawyers breathe better.' Nathalie justifies her impromptu redesign. The comparative adverb 'mieux' modifies the infinitive respirer.
Mathias, tu essaies encore de voler mes clients?
'Mathias, are you still trying to steal my clients?' Andrea accuses Mathias of poaching. The verb 'voler' here colloquially means to poach or steal clients.
J'offre simplement un conseil amical à Nathalie.
'I am simply offering friendly advice to Nathalie.' Mathias denies any underhanded tactics. The adjective 'amical' describes warm friendly support.
Andréa, j'adore votre grande énergie formidable.
'Andrea, I love your great wonderful energy.' Nathalie cushions her upcoming choice. The adjective 'formidable' expresses genuine admiration.
Mais pour ce film, je préfère Camille.
'But for this film, I prefer Camille.' Nathalie selects Camille for her calmer approach. The verb 'preferer' denotes choice between options.
Camille? C'est une excellente idée pour vous!

'Camille? That is an excellent idea for you!' Andrea embraces the decision graciously. The adjective 'excellente' affirms strong agreement. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.
